subject: feral cats
one_liner: Municipal-grade rideshare for feral cats. The vehicle arrives on time. The rider arrives when trust permits.
brand_voice_notes: A transit authority that has mistaken a feral cat for a commuter. Every sentence is a service bulletin. Failure metrics are reported with pride as market realities. Never cute, never winking; the cat is a rider, the alley is a network, patience is infrastructure.

hero.h1: The ride is here. The rider is deciding.
hero.sub: Slink dispatches calm, stationary vehicles to feral cats across 14 metro alley networks. Boarding is voluntary, unscheduled, and statistically rare. We consider this a property of the market, not a flaw in the product.

features.title: Zero-Approach Dispatch
features.blurb: Drivers park at a certified distance, cut the engine, and look at nothing. Onboard sensors log each inch of rider approach as pipeline progress. Most rides close within nine business days.

features.title: Trust-Indexed ETA
features.blurb: Traditional ETAs measure distance. Ours measures willingness. The arrival estimate updates hourly as the rider's confidence rises, collapses, and rises again slightly less than before.

features.title: Dumpster-to-Dumpster Routing
features.blurb: Our route graph maps 40,000 food sources, porch gaps, and warm transformer boxes. Destinations on the Slink network do not need an address. They need a smell.

demo_screen_concept: A live dispatch console for one ride in progress: a stylized CSS/SVG alley map showing the driver parked at the curb and the rider holding position under a porch 40 feet away; a Boarding Confidence meter that creeps upward in real time and collapses when you interact wrong; driver protocol toggles (ENGINE OFF, DOOR AJAR, NO EYE CONTACT) that change the confidence rate; a 'chirp politely' button that immediately costs 30 points of confidence; an event log printing entries like 'Rider observed vehicle from beneath Buick (14 min)'; an ETA that recalculates from 4 minutes to 6 days.

design_direction.style: Swiss-modernist transit-authority service bulletin, daylight signage mode. The page is staged as the route map and service bulletin of a heavily funded mobility company that has decided feral cats are an underserved commuter segment and prices patience by the curb-hour. A cool signage-white ground carries a strict asymmetric grid ruled by hairlines and heavy 2px section rules, the way a transit authority lays out a timetable, so the page reads as posted signage rather than a website. There are no cards and no shadows of any kind: sections are separated by rules, numbered signage chips (RTE 07, STOP 114, FORM S-2), and generous Swiss whitespace; depth comes entirely from type scale, rule weight, and one solid asphalt panel per section. Route-line motifs do the illustration: 3px ink lines with stop dots and a terminus square trace through the hero and between sections, annotated with uppercase mono flags (CURB HOLD, PORCH GAP, TRANSFER). One asphalt near-black carries the wordmark, headlines, rules, signage panels, and all institutional text; one rationed tapetum chartreuse, the exact yellow-green of a cat's eyes in headlights, is reserved strictly for the single primary CTA per section (ink text on chartreuse fill), the live dispatch dot, the boarding-confidence fill, and route highlights, and appears almost nowhere else. Inter Tight at 800 and 900 sets the wordmark and headlines in tight Helvetica-grade caps with timetable confidence; Inter carries plain, faintly regulatory body copy. Every figure that pretends to be dispatch telemetry (boarding confidence, curb-hold hours, ETA ranges, tier prices, attempt counts) is set in Space Mono with tabular figures inside hairline-ruled wells, so it reads like a departures board, not marketing. Motion is timetable-restrained: the dispatch dot pulses on a 3s cycle, route lines draw once on scroll, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, the CTA depresses 1px on press, ETA digits tick like a split-flap board, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No dark mode, no glass, no blur, no clay, no bento cells, no serifs, no offset brutalist shadows, no gradients, no marquee, no emoji. Reads like a transit authority that files a cat's mistrust under 'boarding friction' and posts a six-day wait as on-time performance.
design_direction.archetype: transit-authority service portal: signage hero with route line, numbered feature bulletins, timetable pricing, rider notices as testimonials
design_direction.motion_vocab: timetable-restrained: 3s dispatch-dot pulse, route lines draw once on scroll, 6px fade-rise with 40ms stagger, 1px CTA depress, split-flap ETA digit ticks, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Left-weighted Swiss grid: route chip 'RTE 07' beside the SLINK wordmark top-left; h1 spans eight columns at clamp(3rem, 9vw, 7rem) in Inter Tight 900 caps; a route line with three stop dots labeled CURB, HESITATION, BOARDING runs beneath the hero to a chartreuse terminus square; a live dispatch well top-right holds the pulsing status dot and mono telemetry; the primary CTA is an ink-on-chartreuse signage bar.
